My issue is that the standards you demand from others don’t seem to apply inside your own house. Because when your followers leave your page hating an entire group of people, that isn’t truth. 374e8dc58f49.content: Happy Juneteenth! For those who didn’t grow up in Texas, Juneteenth marks June 19, 1865 — the day enslaved Black Americans in Galveston, Texas finally learned they were free, more than two years after President Abraham Lincoln had signed the Emancipation Proclamation. Juneteenth is a uniquely Texas story that eventually became a national celebration. It’s not just a reminder of slavery, but also of resilience, faith, family, education, and the determination of newly freed Americans to build churches, schools, businesses, and communities despite enormous challenges. Whatever your background, I hope everyone enjoys the holiday and takes a moment to appreciate both the progress that has been made and the opportunities we have to continue building a better future together.
